description: Permission in principal for the erection of 2x dwellings.
decision_conditions: The application site, by reason of its limited dimensions, changes in ground level and close relationship with the retained dwelling at No. 16 Shelley Lane and adjoining residential properties, is unsuitable for the proposed additional residential development. The introduction of two dwellings would result in an unduly cramped form of development, with insufficient separation and space to accommodate the dwellings and associated access works satisfactorily, having regard to the surrounding pattern of development and changes in level, causing harm to the character of the locality and the living conditions of neighbouring occupiers.

These constraints concern the suitability of the site and the proposed amount of development and could not satisfactorily be overcome through detailed design at Technical Details Consent stage. The identified harm would substantially outweigh the benefits of providing two additional homes. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policy D3 of the London Plan (2

The decision to REFUSE permission in principle has been taken having regard to all relevant planning legislation, regulations, guidance, circulars and Council policies, including The Human Rights Act (1998) (HRA 1998) which makes it unlawful for the Council to act incompatibly with Convention rights, specifically Article 6 (right to a fair hearing); Article 8 (right to respect for private and family life); Article 1 of the First Protocol (protection of property) and Article 14 (prohibition of discrimination).

The decision to REFUSE permission in principle has been taken having regard to the policies and proposals in the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012) and Part 2 (2020) set out below, including Supplementary Planning Guidance, and to all relevant material considerations, including The London Plan (2021) and national guidance.

The applicant is advised that, if Permission in Principle is granted on appeal and a subsequent application for Technical Details Consent is approved, the development may be liable for the London Borough of Hillingdon Community Infrastructure Levy (CIL) and the Mayor of London's Community Infrastructure Levy (MCIL).

Any liability would be calculated in accordance with the applicable charging schedules and the Community Infrastructure Levy Regulations 2010 (as amended), including any relevant indexation, exemptions or relief.
Further information is available on the Council's Community Infrastructure Levy webpage and the Mayor of London's Community Infrastructure Levy webpage.
